material_units.source_text: The certificate covers the parameterized part only. An input normalization $x\mapsto\operatorname{diag}(1/s_i)(x-\mu)$ (per-channel standard deviations $s_i\gt0$) is $\max_i(1/s_i)$-Lipschitz, so it multiplies the bound by $\max_i1/s_i$ (Wang & Manchester: about $4.1\gamma$ in pixel space), and last-layer normalization can push the composite constant above the nominal bound, so certified accuracy must be computed with the normalized last layer. Always state the input space in which a radius is measured. (Clean accuracy counts correctly classified unperturbed test inputs; certified accuracy counts those that are also certified at the stated radius; see Primer E.)
